content: If coadministration of a strong CYP3A inhibitor with pirtobrutinib is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose of pirtobrutinib is already 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of the strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A inhibitor has been discontinued for a period equivalent to five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose used prior to the initiation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. Lopinavir increases pitavastatin levels by reducing its metabolism, making this combination contraindicated. Ritonavir increases pitavastatin toxicity through other mechanisms, requiring close monitoring. Additionally, OATP1B1 inhibitors may elevate the risk of myopathy, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ritonavir increases pitolisant levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Lopinavir and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval, and lopinavir also increases pitolisant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE (a CYP3A4 substrate). Ritonavir and lopinavir increase pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Ponatinib levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily and monitor closely. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase posaconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Posaconazole also increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Pralsetinib levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Lopinavir and ritonavir reduce pramlintide effects through other mechanisms, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases pravastatin toxicity through other mechanisms, likely involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. Praziquantel levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Prednisolone and prednisone levels are increased by ritonavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Conversely, prednisone reduces ritonavir and lopinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval, making this combination potentially dangerous. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Primidone reduces ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ritonavir increases prochlorperazine, promethazine, and promethazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Propafenone levels are increased by ritonavir through CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Quazepam levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Quetiapine levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, increasing toxicity risks. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Quinidine levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Quinidine also increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Quinine levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifabutin reduces ritonavir and lopinavir levels. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Rifapentine reduces ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rifaximin levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Rilpivirine also prolongs the QTc interval, increasing toxicity risks. Use caution and monitor closely. Rimegepant levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Riociguat levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition and other mechanisms. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Ripretinib levels are increased by ritonavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition, which may elevate the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. Risperidone levels are increased by ritonavir through CYP2D6 metabolism inhibition and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Rivaroxaban levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. This combination should be avoided due to the increased risk of bleeding. Roflumilast levels are reduced by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP1A2 metabolism induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rosiglitazone effects are reduced by ritonavir and lopinavir, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. Rosuvastatin levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Rucaparib levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Adjust dosages of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated and monitor closely. Ruxolitinib levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Reduce the starting dose to 10 mg twice daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and platelet counts are ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use if platelet counts are <100 x 10^9/L. Sacubitril/valsartan levels are increased by ritonavir through hepatic clearance reduction. Use caution and monitor closely. Salmeterol levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition, increasing toxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. Sarecycline levels are increased by ritonavir through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Monitor for toxicities and adjust dosages as needed. Saxagliptin levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Reduce the dose to 5 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and monitor closely. Seladelpar levels are increased by ritonavir and lopinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely.
